question.problem: Expressed as a decimal in its simplest form, $(5.3)^{2}=${{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
We need to calculate the product of $5.3$ with itself:

$$
{5.3}^{2}=(5.3)\cdot (5.3)
$$

First, we ignore the decimal points and multiply as if both numbers were whole numbers:

$$
\begin{aligned} & \begin{aligned} &  &  & \,\,\,\,\begin{aligned}\boxed{1} \\ \boxed{}\end{aligned}\,\,\,\, &  \\  &  &  & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,\times \,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,3\,\,\,\, \\  &  & \,\,\,\,1\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,\,+\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,6\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,5\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, \\  & \,\,\,\,2\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,8\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,0\,\,\,\, & \,\,\,\,9\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $53\times 53=2\,809.$

We now count the total number of decimal places in the two factors.

There is $1$ decimal place in the first factor ($5.3$) and $1$ decimal place in the second factor ($5.3$), so their product will have $1+1=2$ decimal places.

We take our value of $2\,809$ and insert a decimal point to make a number with $2$ decimal places:

$$
28\,\overset{↓}{.}\,\,\,{{09}_{⏟}}_{2\text{ digits}}
$$

Therefore, ${5.3}^{2}=28.09\,.$
